title: Get Started
text: recent mlts release can installed CRAN via install development version GitHub, need install rstan-package first configure R installation able compile C++ code. can find instructions steps RStan GitHub. Afterwards, can install development version mlts
code: install.packages("mlts") # install.packages("devtools") devtools::install_github("munchfab/mlts")

title: Get Started
text: One simplest models can fit mlts multilevel first order autoregressive model one observed variable. start specifying model mlts_model(). argument q controls number time-series constructs. simple model, following call sufficient: can check parameters present model just calling object: mlts_model() sets model, model parameters free (.e., constrained) default. within level, three fixed effects: grand mean (mu_1) outcome, autoregressive effect (phi(1)_11), natural log innovation variance (ln.sigma2_1). (1) brackets autoregressive effect parameter indicates lag first order, _11 subscript denotes first construct well predicted first construct. Note innovation variance, natural log used prevent variance dropping zero. effects, random effects also estimated level, drawn multivariate normal distribution zero mean. Standard deviations random effects indicated sigma_ prefix, random effect correlations indicated r_ prefix. TeX formula model can obtained calling mlts_model_formula() function model object. default, function produces RMarkdown file renders pdf file using knitr. However, TeX file can also kept calling keep_tex = TRUE within function call. [y1,]=[μ1,]+[y1,itw] \begin{gathered} \begin{bmatrix} y_{1, } \\ \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} \mu_{1,} \\ \end{bmatrix} + \begin{bmatrix} y_{1, }^w \\ \end{bmatrix} \end{gathered} [y1,itw]=[ϕ(1)11,][y1,(t−1)w]+[ζ1,],withζ1,∼𝑁(0,σζ1,i2) \begin{gathered} \begin{bmatrix} y_{1, }^w \\ \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} \phi_{(1)11,} \\ \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} y_{1,(t - 1)}^w \\ \end{bmatrix} +  \begin{bmatrix} \zeta_{1, } \\ \end{bmatrix} ,\\  \text{}~\zeta_{1,} \sim \mathit{N}(0, \sigma^2_{\zeta_{1},})  \end{gathered} [μ1,iϕ(1)11,iln⁡(σζ1,i2)]=[γ0,μ1γ0,ϕ(1)11γ0,ln⁡(σζ12)]+[υμ1,iυϕ(1)11,iυln⁡(σζ12),],withυi∼𝑀𝑉𝑁(𝟎,𝛀) \begin{gathered} \begin{bmatrix} \mu_{1,}\\ \phi_{(1)11,}\\ \ln(\sigma^2_{\zeta_{1},})\\ \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} \gamma_{0,\mu_{1}}\\ \gamma_{0,\phi_{(1)11}}\\ \gamma_{0,\ln(\sigma^2_{\zeta_{1}})}\\ \end{bmatrix} +   \begin{bmatrix} \upsilon_{\mu_{1},}\\ \upsilon_{\phi_{(1)11},}\\ \upsilon_{\ln(\sigma^2_{\zeta_{1}}),}\\ \end{bmatrix} ,\\  \text{}~   \upsilon_{} \sim \mathit{MVN}(\mathbf{0}, \mathbf{\Omega})  \end{gathered} Furthermore, path model can also produced function mlts_paths() many options adjustment.  fit model, pass together data set mlts_fit(). data set example artificial data set simulated autoregressive model: need specify variable data contains time-series process ts argument variable contains unit identifier id argument. argument tinterval, time interval approximation continuous time process can specified Asparouhov et al. (2018). don’t specify , see Vignette Approximation Continuous Time Model details. model summary() shows general information model data: line Time series variables indicated parameter subscripts: 1 --> Y1 shows model parameters indexed _1 refer variable Y1 data set. Model convergence criteria provide overview across convergence diagnostics model parameters (.e., also parameters printed summary() default). simple AR1-model, parameters converged well 4,000 iterations. section Fixed Effects provides information fixed effects model, .e., γ0,μ1\gamma_{0, \mu_1}, γ0,ϕ(1)11\gamma_{0, \phi_{(1)11}}, γ0,ln⁡(σζ12)\gamma_{0,\ln(\sigma^2_{\zeta_{1}})} formula. example, posterior mean autoregressive effect parameter phi(1)_11 estimated .27 95%-credible interval [.22, .33]. log variance innovations ζ1t\zeta_{1t} estimated -.30. section Random Effects SDs shows standard deviations random effects υμ1,\upsilon_{\mu_{1},}, υϕ(1)11,\upsilon_{\phi_{(1)11},}, υln⁡(σζ12),\upsilon_{\ln(\sigma^2_{\zeta_{1}}),}. section Random Effects Correlations shows correlations random effects. example, random effects person mean υμ1,\upsilon_{\mu_{1},} autoregressive effect υϕ(1)11,\upsilon_{\phi_{(1)11},} display nearly correlation, 0.01, positive correlation person mean log innovation variance, 0.22. indicates individuals higher person mean variable Y1 also tend higher innovation variance. parameter estimates can also plotted mlts_plot()-function. default, forest plots model parameters produced. -argument controls parameter types plotted (e.g., fixed effects, random effect standard deviations, ).

(the default option when using mlts_model() and q = 1).  model <- mlts_model(q = 1)   # All model parameters (with their labels stored in model$Param) can be inspected by calling:  model #>                              Model   Level             Type #> mu_1                    Structural  Within     Fixed effect #> phi(1)_11               Structural  Within     Fixed effect #> ln.sigma2_1 Between Random effect SD #> r_mu_1.phi(1)_11        Structural Between   RE correlation #> r_mu_1.ln.sigma2_1      Structural Between   RE correlation #> r_phi(1)_11.ln.sigma2_1 Structural Between   RE correlation #>                                           Param             Param_Label #> mu_1                                       mu_1                   Trait #> phi(1)_11                             phi(1)_11                 Dynamic #> ln.sigma2_1                         ln.sigma2_1 Log Innovation Variance #> sigma_mu_1                           sigma_mu_1                   Trait #> sigma_phi(1)_11                 sigma_phi(1)_11                 Dynamic #> sigma_ln.sigma2_1             sigma_ln.sigma2_1 Log Innovation Variance #> r_mu_1.phi(1)_11               r_mu_1.phi(1)_11                  RE Cor #> r_mu_1.ln.sigma2_1           r_mu_1.ln.sigma2_1                  RE Cor #> r_phi(1)_11.ln.sigma2_1 r_phi(1)_11.ln.sigma2_1                  RE Cor #>                         isRandom prior_type prior_location prior_scale #> mu_1                           1     normal              0        10.0 #> phi(1)_11                      1     normal              0         2.0 #> ln.sigma2_1                    1     normal              0        10.0 #> sigma_mu_1                     0     cauchy              0         2.5 #> sigma_phi(1)_11                0     cauchy 0        LKJ              1          NA #> r_phi(1)_11.ln.sigma2_1        0        LKJ              1          NA   # Possible model extensions/restrictions:  # 1. Introducing additional parameter constraints, such as fixing specific  #    parameters to a constant value by setting the respective random effect  #    variances to zero, such as e.g. (log) innovation variances  model <- mlts_model(q = 1, ranef_zero = "ln.sigma2_1")  #    Note that setting the argument `fix_inno_vars` to `TRUE` provides  #    a shortcut to fixing the innovation variances of all constructs  #    (if q >= 1) to a constant.   # 2. Including a multiple indicator model, where the construct is measured by  #    multiple indicators (here, p = 3 indicators)  model <- mlts_model(           q = 1, # the number of time-varying constructs           p = 3, # the number of manifest indicators           # assuming a common between-level factor (the default)           btw_factor = TRUE         )   # 3. Incorporating between-level variables. For example, inclusion of  #    an additional between-level variable ("cov1") as predictor of all  #    (ranef_pred = "cov1") or a specific set of random effects  #    (ranef_pred = list("phi(1)_11") = "cov1"), an external outcome (e.g., "out1")  #    to be predicted by all (out_pred = "out1") or specific random effects  #    (out_pred = list("out1" = c("etaB_1", "phi(1)_11")), using the latent  #    between-level factor trait scores (etaB_1) and individual first-order  #    autoregressive effects (phi(1)_11) as joint predictors of outcome "out1".  model <- mlts_model(             q = 1,             p = 3,             fix_inno_vars = TRUE,             ranef_pred = "cov1",             out_pred = list("out1" = c("etaB_1", "phi(1)_11"))            )  #    Note that the names of the random effect parameters must match the  #    parameter labels provided in model$Param, the result of the  #    mlts_model()-functions.  # }

title: Reliability estimates for individual model parameters — mlts_rel
text: Reliability conceptualized proportion true individual differences relative total variance, accounting estimation uncertainty. Two methods currently implemented: "EAP": Reliability based posterior mean estimates posterior standard deviations. "RMU": Reliability based repeated random split-half correlations posterior draws, summarized location uncertainty. "EAP" method estimates reliability ratio true score variance total variance, total variance decomposed -person variability posterior mean estimates expected posterior uncertainty (measurement error). Specifically, reliability defined $$ Rel = \frac{Var(\hat{\theta})}{Var(\hat{\theta}) + E(SE^2)} $$ \(\hat{\theta}\) denotes posterior mean (EAP) estimates individual parameters \(SE\) posterior standard deviations. formulation follows conceptualization reliability proportion variance observed estimates reflects stable -person differences, rather estimation uncertainty. "RMU" method implements resampling-based approach quantify reliability individual differences model parameters. Posterior draws repeatedly split independent subsets, correlations subsets computed across individuals. split-half correlations provide estimate stability (replicability) individual differences posterior uncertainty. resulting distribution correlations summarized obtain point estimates uncertainty intervals (equal-tailed credible intervals) reliability. approaches explicitly account uncertainty individual parameter estimation designed intensive longitudinal data, reliability pertains stability individual-specific model parameters rather observed variables. "RMU" implementation described : Bignardi, G., Kievit, R. ., & Bürkner, P.C. (2025), general method estimating reliability using Bayesian Measurement Uncertainty, PsyArXiv. https://osf.io/preprints/psyarxiv/h54k8_v1
